title: 2014 HMMT February Guts Problem 18
statement: Find the number of ordered quadruples of positive integers \((a, b, c, d)\) such that \(a, b, c\), and \(d\) are all (not necessarily distinct) factors of 30 and \(a b c d>900\).

solutions.text: 1940 Since \(a b c d>900 \Longleftrightarrow \frac{30}{a} \frac{30}{b} \frac{30}{c} \frac{30}{d}<900\), and there are \(\binom{4}{2}^{3}\) solutions to \(a b c d=2^{2} 3^{2} 5^{2}\), the answer is \(\frac{1}{2}\left(8^{4}-\binom{4}{2}^{3}\right)=1940\) by symmetry.
